blocks.text: In the beginning, God creates the heavens and the earth. The initial creation-scene presents the earth as formless, empty, and shrouded in darkness. Into this scene of unordered chaos, the Spirit of God moves—an active divine presence that will accomplish the ordering to follow. This opening establishes both creation's absolute dependence on God and the Spirit's role in shaping what emerges.

God's culminating creative act brings forth humanity—male and female—made in the image of God. This language denotes not physical form but representative vocation: humans bear God's character and authority, appointed as stewards of the earth. God blesses them with fruitfulness and commissions them to have dominion over all living creatures. Humanity is the crown of creation, bearing responsibility for the world entrusted to them, yet remaining creatures accountable to their Creator.

Genesis 1 culminates when God rests on the seventh day. This rest is not idleness but the completion of creation and its evaluation. The cosmos is declared not merely good in its parts but very good in its totality—a finished, coherent whole established by God's sovereign design. The seventh day is blessed and set apart, establishing a rhythm of work and rest that reflects creation's own order and anticipates the rhythm that will structure Israel's life.
